title: Prohibition and a century of American drinking (1920)

steps.claim: National Prohibition takes effect under the Volstead Act

test.source: Eighteenth Amendment in force 17 Jan 1920

steps.claim: Drinking falls by roughly a third and deaths from cirrhosis fall with it

test.source: Miron & Zwiebel (1991): consumption fell to 30–40% of its pre-Prohibition level at first, recovering to 60–70% by 1933; cirrhosis deaths among men fell from about 30 per 100,000 in 1911 to about 11 in 1929

steps.link_why: the economists' reconstruction from cirrhosis, arrests and psychosis admissions

steps.claim: Bootlegging feeds organized crime; the homicide rate climbs from under 7 to nearly 10 per 100,000

test.source: St. Valentine's Day Massacre, 14 Feb 1929; homicide rates from Eckberg (1995) and Historical Statistics of the United States

steps.link_why: historians and the Wickersham Commission (1931) tied the growth of gang crime to the illegal trade

steps.claim: Al Capone is convicted of tax evasion

test.source: US District Court, Chicago, 17 Oct 1931

steps.link_why: the bootlegging fortune was the income the charges rested on

steps.claim: The Twenty-first Amendment repeals Prohibition

test.source: Ratified 5 Dec 1933 (Cullen–Harrison Act had allowed 3.2% beer from 7 Apr 1933)

steps.link_why: the repeal campaign argued from enforcement failure, crime and lost tax revenue (AAPA; Wickersham Commission)

steps.claim: Alcoholics Anonymous is founded in Akron

test.source: Bill W. and Dr. Bob, 10 Jun 1935

steps.note: Eighteen months after repeal. No document ties the founding to repeal; the Oxford Group and the founders' own histories do. Plausible, not shown.

steps.claim: Per-capita drinking climbs back for half a century and peaks around 1980
steps.link_why: the national series itself; repeal is the start of the climb

steps.claim: Cirrhosis deaths peak in the early 1970s

test.source: NCHS vital statistics: age-adjusted cirrhosis mortality peaked in 1973 at about 15 per 100,000

steps.note: Deaths peaked seven years before per-capita drinking did, because the heaviest drinkers were an older cohort; ordered here against repeal.

steps.claim: The Hughes Act creates the National Institute on Alcohol Abuse and Alcoholism

test.source: Comprehensive Alcohol Abuse and Alcoholism Prevention, Treatment, and Rehabilitation Act, signed 31 Dec 1970

steps.link_why: Senator Harold Hughes, a recovering alcoholic and AA member, wrote the Act; the AMA had called alcoholism a disease in 1956. Ordered against AA's founding.

steps.claim: Teen drinking falls for four decades: 12th-graders who drank in the past month, 72% (1980) → 50% (2000) → 29% (2019)

test.source: Monitoring the Future, University of Michigan, annual 12th-grade past-30-day alcohol use

steps.link_why: the survey series itself; the decline begins at the 1980 peak

steps.claim: Young adults follow: under-35s who drink, 72% (2001–03) → 62% (2021–23); in 2025 only 54% of all adults drink, the lowest Gallup has recorded

test.source: Gallup Consumption Habits surveys; 2025 release 13 Aug 2025

steps.claim: Non-alcoholic beer becomes a real category, growing about 30% a year

test.source: NielsenIQ off-premise sales 2022–23; Athletic Brewing founded 2017

steps.link_why: trade data; the brewers themselves cite younger drinkers

steps.claim: Most US teens have a smartphone

test.source: Pew Research, Teens, Social Media and Technology 2015: 73% of teens have a smartphone

steps.claim: Claim: smartphones started the teen decline

test.source: Pew: the year a majority of US teens had a smartphone (2012)

steps.note: The decline began some thirty years before most teens had a smartphone. As the origin, busted; as an accelerant after 2012, open. Dated when the claimed cause arrived; tested against the decline's onset, the 1980 peak in Monitoring the Future.

steps.claim: Dry January begins as a public campaign

test.source: Alcohol Change UK (then Alcohol Concern), first campaign January 2013

steps.claim: Claim: Dry January started the decline

test.source: Alcohol Change UK: the first Dry January campaign, January 2013

steps.note: Thirty-two years too late to be the origin; a plausible accelerant for adults after 2013. Dated when the claimed cause arrived; tested against the decline's onset, the 1980 peak in Monitoring the Future.

steps.claim: Legal recreational cannabis begins (Colorado)

test.source: Colorado retail sales from 1 Jan 2014

steps.claim: Claim: legal cannabis started the decline

test.source: Colorado's first retail cannabis sales, Jan 1, 2014

steps.note: Too late to be the origin; substitution among adults after 2014 is an open question with mixed evidence. Dated when the claimed cause arrived; tested against the decline's onset, the 1980 peak in Monitoring the Future.

steps.claim: Sober Curious is published and names a movement

test.source: Ruby Warrington, Sober Curious, HarperOne, 31 Dec 2018

steps.claim: Attention to 'sober curious' rises after the book
The Surgeon General calls for cancer warnings on alcohol

test.source: Surgeon General's advisory on alcohol and cancer risk, 3 Jan 2025

steps.claim: Claim: the cancer warning drove the 2025 record low

test.source: The Surgeon General's advisory on alcohol and cancer, Jan 3, 2025

steps.note: Dated when the advisory came out; tested against the under-35 decline already visible in Gallup's 2021–23 pooled surveys. Busted as a cause of the trend; it may shape what people say about it.

steps.claim: Per-capita drinking falls for two decades after the 1981 peak

test.source: NIAAA apparent per-capita ethanol consumption, gallons per person 14 and older, 1970–2022

steps.note: The NIAAA series begins in 1970, so the climb after repeal cannot be tested in it; the fall from the 1981 peak (2.76 gallons) to the 1990s (2.15) can, as a two-year change from 1982 against every other two-year change in the series.

steps.claim: Young adults in legal-cannabis states drink less than elsewhere (the dose-response test)
steps.note: Dose-response, first rung above timing: in the 20 states that opened retail cannabis (2014–2023), past-30-day drinking among adults 18–24 (CDC BRFSS) changed by about the same as in the 31 states that never did; the pre-registered youth outcome (YRBS) could not be run because the state tables end in 2017 and Colorado and Washington do not take part. Protocol: ripples/docs/dose_response_v1.md.

steps.claim: Attention to alcohol and cancer surges after the Surgeon General's advisory
Dry January draws a January surge every year
steps.note: A seasonal rise: placebo windows that fall in other Januaries make the test honest about that. Checked at the Jan 2018 campaign (daily views begin Jul 2015; Jan 2017 left fewer than 20 placebo windows).
